identity: Politician and political activist · South Africa · 1918–2013
title: Nelson Mandela's birth chart
metaDescription: Nelson Mandela's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.0° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.9° separates Mercury and Saturn from an exact conjunction; at that range thinking and structure read as one mechanism. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 25.0° Cancer — deep enough in the third decan (20°–30°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 15.9° Leo, Venus was at 22.4° Gemini, Mars was at 12.5° Libra. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction that begins as conversation; effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mercury and Saturn — a conjunction holding at 0.9°. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Mars sextile Saturn at 2.5°, and Mercury sextile Mars at 3.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Sun makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Moon in Scorpio at 18.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Libra at 12.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Cancer at 1.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Leo at 15.0° is in detriment. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 4, fire 3, air 3 across the elements, and fixed 5, cardinal 4, mutable 1 across the modalities. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 18.8°.
